qualificationStatus: Diagnostic reproduced the original menu-click timeout. It is not a pass or a replacement for the failed restoration gate.
findings: The first menu opening succeeded with trusted pointer/click delivery and stable menu geometry.
The second menu opening reproduced the unchanged3000ms timeout while the menu remained visible, enabled, unobstructed and geometrically stable. Boot was ready and no modal was open.

A4013ms self long task overlapped the failed attempt; RAF sampling paused for approximately4seconds. No pointerdown, mousedown or click was observed for the failed attempt, so this reproduction did not reach the menu click handler.

This establishes main-thread starvation before input dispatch for the instrumented reproduction. It does not identify the owning application function, prove the source of the earlier Firefox failure, or justify a longer timeout.
limitations: The read-only geometry/event observer can perturb timing; diagnostic copies and hashes are preserved for review.
Long Task API attribution identifies self/main-frame only and has no JavaScript call stack. A bounded CPU sample during the same interval is the narrow next step if authorized.
No production or durable qualifier changes, forced click, alternate key, timeout increase or retry of the qualification receipt occurred.
